title: Uv Editor Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive

markdown_content: ## Overview of UV Editor Location and Access in CLO 2025.0 This section explains the updated location and access method for the UV editor in CLO 2025.0, important for managing UV maps and preparing garments for export to other 3D software. The UV editor in CLO 2025.0 has been relocated to the top toolbar under **Materials > UV > UV Editor**. Users can open the UV editor window from this menu and resize it for better visibility. This editor displays all pattern pieces arranged within the UV space, allowing users to view and modify UV layouts. Users can select all pattern pieces and apply **auto UV packing** to efficiently arrange them within the 0 to 1 UV tile space. This ensures proper layout for texture mapping and export. --- ## Managing Pattern Pieces and Fabric Sides in the UV Editor This section details how to select individual pattern pieces in the UV editor and configure export settings for fabric sides (front, back, side), essential for accurate material mapping on garments with multiple fabric layers. Pattern pieces can be individually selected within the UV editor. For fabrics with different materials on the inside (such as linings) or double-sided materials, users can control which sides are displayed and exported. In the **Property Editor** panel (make sure the Property Editor is active), scroll to the bottom to find options for exporting fabric sides: - **Back Face**: Enable to include the back side of the fabric in the export. - **Side Face**: Enable to include the side edge of the fabric in the export. These options allow exporting both front and back textures for lining fabrics or shell fabrics that have distinct back and front materials. This is critical for workflows requiring detailed texture maps for all visible surfaces of a garment. --- ## Exporting UV Maps and Snapshots This section covers how to export UV maps and snapshots from the UV editor for use in external 3D software or texture editing. After setting up the UV layout and fabric side export options, users can capture a **snapshot** of the UV map or export it in various file formats supported by CLO. To export: 1. Take a snapshot within the UV editor. 2. Choose the desired file format for export. 3. Save the file to the appropriate directory path. This process ensures all UV maps and material maps are saved correctly for further use in other 3D applications, preserving details such as wrinkling and fabric orientation. --- ## Summary of Improvements CLO 2025.0 introduces several key improvements to the UV editor: - Relocated UV editor access for streamlined workflow. - Enhanced pattern piece selection with ability to toggle export of back and side fabric faces. - Improved export capabilities including snapshots and multiple file formats. - Support for managing complex fabric setups such as linings and double-sided materials. These updates facilitate better preparation of garment UV maps for external software and provide more control over material exports, enhancing the overall 3D garment design pipeline.
